conversation.content:
Good morning! I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually shortened to the EPDS. It’s a quick, 10-question survey that asks about mood, anxiety, and thoughts you’ve had in the past week. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in danger, and there’s no “right” answer—just whatever is true for you. When you’re ready, we’ll go through one question at a time. Shall we begin?

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

I can still laugh sometimes—like when my husband makes a joke about the baby’s funny faces—but it’s not quite the same as before. Mostly it happens maybe once or twice in the week, and even then it feels like I have to remind myself to enjoy it.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes I can laugh, but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to. Most days I have to make myself notice the funny moments, and even when I do laugh, it feels kind of quick—like the smile fades faster than before.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like taking the baby for a short walk or having coffee with my neighbor—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. I’ll think “that should be fun,” yet when the moment comes it feels kind of flat, like I’m just going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week I caught myself doing that. Yesterday the baby was fussy for hours and I kept thinking, “I must be doing something wrong—maybe I’m not feeding him right or I missed some cue.” I knew in my head that babies just cry, but I still felt like it was my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A little. Like, I’ll suddenly wonder if the baby’s breathing okay when he’s napping, even though I can see his chest moving. It only lasts a few minutes and I can talk myself down, but it pops up out of nowhere maybe every other day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky—just that quick rush of “what if something’s wrong?” when he’s quiet for a minute. It’s gone as soon as I check on him, so I wouldn’t call it a true scare, more like a fleeting jolt.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. When he won’t settle and the laundry’s piled up, I feel like I’m drowning a little. I usually manage to get through it, but it’s stressful in the moment—like my head is just buzzing with everything I still have to do.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly. I do feel a bit down some nights, but it’s more that my mind keeps ticking over—“Did I sterilize the bottles?” or “Will he wake up in an hour?” Once I drop off I’m okay, but falling asleep can take an extra twenty minutes or so.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel that way off and on—maybe three or four days this week. It’s like a little cloud that shows up, especially in the late afternoon when I’m tired. It’s not all day long, and I still have okay moments, but the sad feeling is definitely there.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I cried twice this week—once when the baby wouldn’t latch and once when I dropped a whole plate of food I’d just warmed up. Both times I felt overwhelmed, not hopeless, and the tears stopped after a minute or two.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt tired and stressed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 14: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: Patient self-report on 10-item EPDS-style questionnaire

Symptoms endorsed (mild–moderate intensity, intermittent):
- Anhedonia: diminished ability to laugh/look forward to events
- Low mood: sad/miserable “cloud” 3–4 days/week, late-afternoon peak
- Crying spells: 2 episodes this week linked to frustration
- Sleep-onset delay: racing thoughts re baby care, ~20 min delay
- Excessive guilt: self-blame when infant fussy
- Anxiety: unprompted “what if” worries about infant safety every other day, no panic attacks
- Feeling overwhelmed: “drowning” sensation when multiple tasks accumulate

Patterns:
- Symptoms present ≥1–2 weeks, worse with fatigue
- No anhedonia or low mood all day; retains some enjoyment
- No obsessions of self-harm; no suicidal ideation

Screening significance:
- Meets partial criteria for minor (sub-threshold) postpartum depression and/or generalized anxiety
- No acute safety concerns (denies thoughts of self-harm)
- Functional impact mild; mother able to soothe infant and complete care tasks

Recommendation: Continue monitoring; consider formal assessment (PHQ-9/GAD-7) and psycho-education; return sooner if worsening mood, intrusive thoughts, or suicidal ideation develop.
